data_section_full_text:
Section 16 of the Securities and Exchange Act of 1934 defines a class of persons
designated as insiders whose trades are subject to specific limitations and reporting
requirements. The insider-trading data were collected from the Dow Jones News
Retrieval Service by downloading the daily newswire covering SEC filings published by Federal Filings, Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of Dow Jones & Co.,
Inc. The insider-trading records cover transactions by section 16 insiders during
the period August 1993 to October 1998. Our empirical analyses are limited to
trades occurring in fiscal years 1994 to 1997.


CAR Vol. 24 No. 1 (Spring 2007)

200 Contemporary Accounting Research


We exclude certain types of transactions from the analysis.
